This is retained producer evidence, without live browser transaction IDs, scenario provenance, execution attribution or deployment authenticity. Recorded URLs are never fetched.
Every record is decoded before selection; no partial success is returned on malformed input or a resource limit.
Known authentication headers/cookies and explicitly marked literal values are excluded. Unknown extension names do not establish sensitivity.

Complete evidence is bounded by a 33554432-byte input budget, a 100663296-byte reply budget, and a 64-level nesting cap. Set max_input_bytes, max_reply_bytes or max_nesting_depth explicitly for the next call to change those budgets without restarting REA. capture_timeout_ms is 30000 ms (omitted means 30000). HAR/SAZ/qlog use a 192 MiB Node old-generation heap (source default). The effective REA_CAPTURE_DECODER_OLD_GENERATION_MIB value is 192 MiB (source default; default 192 MiB, floor 8 MiB, maximum 16384 MiB). On Node.js the decoder passes --max-old-space-size=192 and removes inherited NODE_OPTIONS, so additional host memory and NODE_OPTIONS do not raise this heap. The 8 MiB semi-space stays fixed. On Bun the V8 flags are ignored. Windows limits the decoder's committed memory to this value plus a 512 MiB reserve. Other Bun hosts enforce no decoder heap limit. Set REA_CAPTURE_DECODER_OLD_GENERATION_MIB in the environment that starts the next REA invocation. It must be a decimal integer from 8 to 16384. Mitmproxy decoding uses a 768 MiB Linux address-space limit.
